title: Product Owner (Enterprise Systems)
description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION

The Community Foundation of Singapore (CFS) is a non-profit organisation founded in 2008 to encourage and enable philanthropy in Singapore.

We match donors' interests with causes and offer ways for them to make a greater impact through their charitable funds. We also collaborate with charity partners to identify programmes that support diverse communities.

Our purpose is to enable real and meaningful change while inspiring a philanthropic culture in Singapore. CFS is a registered charity with Institution of a Public Character status.

For more information, visit www.cf.org.sg

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the business value delivered by the product. This includes owning the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and backlog, and shaping business priorities across product-enabled processes.

The role focuses on the "why", "what" and "when" of the product — value outcomes, user experience, and prioritization — while partnering with product administrators, developers, and integration teams on the "how" of solution delivery. The Product Owner also ensures appropriate approval and governance of product changes based on risk, compliance, and business impact.

Key Responsibilities

1) Own Product Vision, Strategy & Roadmap

  • Define and communicate the product vision, goals, and success measures (e.g., data accuracy and integrity, error rates, automation levels, cycle times, user adoption).
  • Align product strategy with business objectives, operating model, and technology standards.
  • Maintain and socialize a multi-year product roadmap, including sequencing, dependencies, and expected value outcomes.

2) Backlog & Pipeline Ownership

  • Own, prioritize, and continuously refine the product backlog/pipeline to maximize value, balancing regulatory/compliance needs, risk reduction, technical health, and business outcomes.
  • Ensure backlog items are well-defined (scope, dependencies, non-functional requirements where relevant, and acceptance criteria) and transparent to stakeholders and delivery teams.
  • Define and maintain working agreements (e.g., Definition of Ready, Definition of Done), including UAT approach and sign-off criteria.

3) Translate Business Needs into Functional Solutions

  • Lead discovery with business stakeholders to understand pain points, define desired outcomes, and translate needs into user stories / functional requirements with measurable acceptance criteria.
  • Drive functional solution decisions (e.g., configure vs. customize vs. integrate) in partnership with technical SMEs, optimizing for speed, operational efficiency, maintainability, security/auditability, and total cost of ownership.
  • Own functional standards for the product (e.g., common ways of working, master data rules) and manage exceptions through agreed governance.

4) Partner with Product Admins, Developers & Integration Teams

  • Collaborate closely with product administrators, developers, integration teams, and vendors to deliver changes (configuration, scripting, reporting, integrations, etc.).
  • Review technical solution designs to ensure alignment to business intent and standards.
  • Coordinate UAT and functional sign-off; confirm release readiness, including training, communications, support handover, and documentation.

5) Drive Data Integrity & Process Consistency (Business Ownership)

  • Define and maintain business rules, controls, and process standards to drive consistency across subsidiaries/business units and prevent one-off decisions that reduce scalability and reporting integrity.
  • Partner with process owners to drive the process changes needed to fully leverage product capabilities, improve productivity, and reduce operational and control risks.
  • Partner with administrators to ensure role-based access, segregation of duties, and validations that will enable clean operations and compliant reporting.
  • Own or co-own master data standards (e.g., customers, vendors, items, chart of accounts) and champion data quality practices with business/process owners.

6) Data, Architecture & User Experience (UX) Stewardship

  • Champion a user-centric approach to product decisions, ensuring that workflows, interfaces, and content are intuitive, accessible, and aligned to how end users actually work.
  • Define and maintain UX guidelines and patterns for the product (e.g., navigation standards, form layouts, error messaging, terminology) in partnership with design and technical teams.
  • Leverage qualitative and quantitative data (e.g., usage analytics, funnel/drop-off analysis, CSAT/NPS, support tickets, time-on-task) to identify pain points and opportunities to simplify and streamline the user experience.
  • Establish and manage feedback loops with end users (e.g., interviews, surveys, usability testing, beta programs, office hours) and translate insights into clear product requirements and backlog items.
  • Define, track, and report experience-focused KPIs (e.g., task completion rates, user adoption, time to complete key flows, error/rework rates) and incorporate findings into roadmap and prioritization decisions.
  • Partner with data and analytics lead to align product data models, integrations, and reporting structures with target-state data architecture and reference architectures.
  • Define and maintain conceptual and logical data views for the product (e.g., key entities, relationships, and flows) to support scalable integrations, analytics, and downstream systems.
  • Ensure that data captured through the product (e.g., required fields, validation rules, defaults, and reference data) balances user effort with downstream needs for reporting, analytics, and controls.
  • Own or contribute to data management practices for the product, including data lifecycle rules (creation, updates, retention, archival), data ownership, and stewardship responsibilities across business teams.
  • Partner with data, analytics, and reporting teams to align on metric definitions, critical data elements, and master/transactional data usage, ensuring data is fit for purpose and enabling self-service insights where possible.
  • Support compliance with data-related policies (e.g., privacy, retention, protection, segregation of data) by ensuring product features, configurations, and processes reflect required controls.

7) Stakeholder Management & Governance

  • Identify, engage, and manage stakeholders to align priorities, manage expectations, and secure required sponsorship and sign-offs.
  • Act as the primary point of contact and decision facilitator for product demand, providing clear rationale for prioritization decisions.
  • Establish and operate governance practices (intake, prioritization forums, approval thresholds, release cadence, and change control) to ensure a stable, transparent, and auditable change pipeline.
  • Oversee user enablement (training materials, communications, office hours) to drive adoption and effective use of the product.

8) Release, Testing, and Change Management

  • Plan releases with delivery teams; coordinate UAT; publish release notes; and drive training and adoption for product changes and vendor updates.
  • Provide post-release hypercare, triage issues, and prioritize fixes and enhancements.
  • Track and report outcomes after go-live (e.g., adoption, time savings, defect trends, control effectiveness, user feedback) and feed insights into backlog prioritization and roadmap refinement.
QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 3 - 5 years of relevant experience in product ownership, business analysis, project management, or process improvement.
  • Demonstrated experience managing product roadmaps and backlogs and delivering cross-functional system or process changes.
  • Experience working with business stakeholders, technology teams, vendors, and governance forums.
  • Experience with Agile or hybrid delivery methods.
  • Experience with NetSuite is advantageous.

Skills

  • Product strategy, roadmap development, and value-based prioritization.
  • Business analysis, requirements elicitation, user story development, acceptance criteria definition and process re-engineering.
  • Backlog management, release planning, UAT coordination, and change management.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to translate business needs into practical functional solutions in collaboration with technical teams.
  • Analytical and problem-solving capability, including the use of data and user insights to guide decisions.
  • Working knowledge of data governance, internal controls, access management, system integrations, and user experience principles.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to present complex issues to business and technical audiences.

OTHER INFORMATION

The Right-of-Way Supervisor leads a team of right-of-way agents and field personnel on assigned project spreads — setting daily direction, holding the team to Gray Hawk’s standards, and making sure acquisitions move on schedule, on budget and with clean, defensible documentation. This role is the field link between the agents and the Project Manager, and represents the client, Gray Hawk and the team with professionalism and integrity.

Core Responsibilities
• Supervise and lead the right-of-way agents, land negotiators, field personnel and third-party contractors assigned to the project spread — assign work, set expectations and review results.
• Hold the team to the Gray Hawk Proactive Standard: after first contact, agents actively pursue landowners rather than waiting; voicemail-and-wait is acceptable only on the first attempt.
• Make sure every landowner contact is documented in the project’s land-management database the day it happens.
• Negotiate the more complex surface use agreements, easements and pipeline rights-of-way; settle surface damages and secure access to client assets.
• Review agents’ agreements and documentation for accuracy before they go to the Project Manager or the client.
• Track timelines and budgets for the spread, prepare status reports, and coordinate directly with the Project Manager and the client.
• Establish and maintain good relationships with surface owners, local government officials and agencies; de-escalate tense situations quickly.
• Conduct or direct internal and courthouse title research; interpret and redline alignment drawings, certified property plats, permit drawings, temporary workspace drawings and construction access drawings.
• Lead the team’s field safety: walk each new team member through the Field Safety Manual and Safety Training and complete the sign-off with them; hold the daily safety briefing and keep the Daily Safety Log.
• Coach and develop agents, and address performance issues promptly.

Success Metrics
• Every agent working under clear assignments and to the Gray Hawk Proactive Standard.
• Landowner contacts documented the same day, across the whole team.
• No unresolved escalations aging beyond 3 days without documented status.
• Acquisition milestones for the spread met on schedule.
• Zero material documentation errors on executed agreements.
• No team member working alone in the field before their Field Safety acknowledgment and Safety Training sign-off are complete.

Required Qualifications
• Minimum five (5) years of right-of-way experience, primarily negotiating easements for pipelines.
• Minimum three (3) years supervising right-of-way agents.
• Proven ability to lead a large team of agents and field personnel — setting direction, reviewing work and holding people to a standard.
• Leadership experience on FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline projects.
• Texas pipeline experience, including work with the Texas Railroad Commission.
• Working knowledge of Texas condemnation (eminent domain) law and procedure for pipelines.
• Thorough understanding of surface use agreements, easements, pipeline ROW, surface title, and the laws and regulations governing right-of-way work in Texas.
• Ability to conduct internal and courthouse title research without supervision.
• Mapping-software experience (GIS, Google Earth; deed plotting) and the ability to learn client mapping systems.
• Experience with land-management databases (such as Irth Land Management or comparable) and the ability to learn new client databases quickly.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel).
• Valid driver’s license.
• Must supply their own mobile phone that can receive email, and a computer capable of doing the job effectively.
• Bachelor’s degree preferred; equivalent right-of-way experience or IRWA certification (SR/WA or RW/AC) accepted in its place.
• Available to start within weeks of an offer and to work on-site in the Permian Basin.

Preferred Qualifications
• IRWA certification (SR/WA or RW/AC).
• Experience with ESRI GIS software.
• Experience across multiple asset types (pipeline, electric transmission, renewables).

Pay and Benefits
Competitive pay, per diem, and full health, vision and dental benefits; details discussed during interviews.
Don’t meet every requirement? If you have strong FERC pipeline leadership experience but not in Texas, we still want to hear from you.

title: Project Coordinator
description:

title: Plate Fitter 1st Class - Night Shift
description:
Plate Fitter 1st Class - Night Shift

We are seeking an experienced Night Shift Plate Fitter to join our team. The ideal candidate will have previous shipyard or heavy industrial experience, a strong commitment to safety and quality, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced production environment. Candidates must be dependable, team-oriented, and available to work the night shift and overtime as needed.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

This position is responsible for the following: Other duties may be assigned.

  1. Must have a basic understanding of mathematics and be able to perform operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, as well as work fractions.
  2. Ability to interpret blueprints and perform lay outs and fabricate metal structural parts, such as plates, bulkheads, and frames, and braces them in position within hull of ship for riveting or welding.
  3. Quality Control: before using verify material compatibility with specifications.
  4. Lays out position of parts on metal, working from blueprints or templates and using scribe and hand tools.
  5. Locates and marks reference lines, such as center, buttock, and frame lines.
  6. Positions parts in hull of ship, assisted by Rigger.
  7. Align parts in relation to each other, using jacks, turnbuckles, clips, wedges, and mauls.
  8. Marks location of holes to be drilled and installs temporary fasteners to hold part in place for welding or riveting.
  9. Install packing, gaskets, liners, and structural accessories and members, such as doors, hatches, brackets, and clips.
  10. May prepare molds and templates for fabrication of nonstandard parts.

  11. Remove high spots and cut bevels, using hand files, portable grinders and cutting torches.

  12. May tack weld clips and brackets in place prior to permanent welding.
  13. May roll, bend, flange, cut, and shape plates, beams, and other heavy metal parts, using shop machinery, such as plate rolls, presses, bending brakes, and joggle machines.
  14. Safely and efficiently use various hand, power and cutting tools.

  15. Be able to use large machinery such as a metal shear, metal brake and band saw.

Required Education & Experience:

  1. High School Diploma and/or one year certificate from college or technical school preferred.

  2. Must be able to pass a hands-on test when applicable and/or marine/industrial plate/structural fitting experience:

  • 1st Class: 3-5 years

  • 2nd Class: 1-3 years

Working Conditions:

  1. Open-air conditions such as noisy, hot, cold, etc.
  2. Must wear hearing, eye, head protection and proper PPE.
  3. Some climbing (100 feet) and lifting (50 lbs.) involved.
  4. Traverse gangways and scaffolding at varying heights while wearing fall prevention equipment.
  5. Working with hot and sometimes hazardous materials.
  6. Aboard ships, both on and offshore as well as confined spaces.
  7. Must be able to stand and operate equipment for up to four continuous hours.
  8. The work requires long periods of sitting in awkward positions, standing on a variety of surfaces and at differing angles, bending over, crouching, and climbing up and over obstructions such as scaffolding, ladders, and internal barge and boat structural members.

Necessary Equipment Operation:

  1. Cutting Torch
  2. Squares
  3. Levels
  4. Hand and Power Tools

Special Skills:

  1. Ability to work under deadlines and schedule pressures.
  2. Ability to read and interpret blueprints, sketches, drawings, and technical manuals.
  3. Perform basic mathematical functions.
  4. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  5. High performance and a strong team player.
  6. Commitment to company values and safety program.
